text:
marta: Quick proposal re: failover behavior for tenants with strict data-residency. Problem: full active/active swap can unintentionally surface non-local data during fast failovers. Want to discuss a deferred-fallback model.

kevin: TL;DR for deferred-fallback?

marta: Idea: on route failure, instead of immediately switching to remote primary, we attempt a 3-tier degradable path: 1) local degraded mode (serve cached/readonly), 2) soft remote (serve responses with residency headers + PII-mask), 3) full remote routing. Each step has timers + audit events.

nina: Nice. That maps to product tiers: Dedicated tenants can opt into "strict-local-first". Hosted can default to soft-remote unless customer requests stricter.

infra-bot: config.apply request: set policy.deferred_fallback.default=soft-remote -> accepted for staging.

kevin: Two implementation questions: where to enforce PII-mask? edge-proxy or model-serving? Masking at edge is safer but might be lossy.

marta: Prefer edge-proxy mask for speedy guarantees + single place to audit, but add a flag so model-serving can override when semantic masking is available.

alisa: For KV-owned caches, we need a hint: cache.owner_region + cache.staleness_ms. If we serve cached local result, emit cache.served=true and residency.breach=false.

nina: Also need client-visible headers so integrators can decide: X-Redwood-Residency-Status: local|soft-remote|remote and X-Redwood-Residency-Note for masking.

kevin: Ops-safety: require a two-way handshake before step 3. Control-plane must write a lease_transfer intent and observe a confirmation heartbeat from remote before cutting over. That prevents mid-swap race.

marta: Example control flow snippet: 
```
1. detect degraded-local
2. attempt local-readonly (TTL=30s) -> emit event: fallback.attempt=local
3. if not healed within backoff (t1) -> attempt soft-remote with masking -> fallback.attempt=soft_remote
4. if remote confirmed healthy + handshake OK -> do lease_transfer -> fallback.attempt=remote
```

qa-bot: checklist added: run chaos: network-partition, kv-eviction, pod-oom. Acceptance: no residency.breach=true emitted for strict-local tenants.

kevin: Telemetry: emit residency_switch_attempts, residency_final_state, fallback_latency_ms, masking_applied boolean. Dashboards needed per-tenant.

nina: Legal asked for an audit trail. We should write residency.audit events to an append-only store (retain 90d for Hosted, 365d for Dedicated).

marta: Edge cases: a) cold cache + masked soft-remote might degrade UX, b) customers with zero-tolerance may prefer fail-open=false which returns 503 instead. Need per-tenant policy.

kevin: Perf note: soft-remote path should prefer compressed responses and avoid large embeddings fetches. Maybe serve a short summary instead of full length during soft-remote.

infra-bot: experiment flag created: feature.deferred_fallback.v1 -> staging rollout (20%).

alisa: I'll add the cache.owner_region tag and kv_cache.staleness_ms metric. Also add logs: `residency=soft_remote reason=cache_miss`

marta: Proposed rollout steps: 1) config + headers + telemetry, 2) edge-proxy masking + audit write, 3) staged chaos tests, 4) RFC to opt-in Dedicated defaults and Hosted opt-outs.

kevin: +1. Please include migration plan for existing tenants that rely on immediate remote failover. We need a toggle to opt-in old behavior.

nina: I'll draft the RFC and include policy YAML example: 
```
residency_policy: {
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "failover_mode": "deferred",        # deferred | immediate | deny
  "soft_remote_masking": true,
  "deny_on_breach": false
}
```

marta: Cool. Action items: nina will draft RFC, alisa adds cache tags + logs, kevin prototypes lease-handshake, I (marta) will wire headers and tests. I'll open a tracking PR and tag the list.

kevin: Add an integration test that asserts `X-Redwood-Residency-Status` transitions and that no residency.audit with breach=true exists for strict tenants under simulated partitions.

marta: Thanks. I'll create the PR now and ping this thread. :rocket:
